title: Choose the visual world for MiniCloud
question: The roll assigned Cloud Atlas Plate. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Cloud Atlas Plate
options.lineage: Luke Howard's cloud classification and the WMO International Cloud Atlas — scientific specimen plates, not weather apps
options.thesis: Your files are a collection under observation, not rows in a storage console. MiniCloud reads the name literally in the one way nobody expects: cloud *classification*, not cloud computing. It refuses the SaaS storage dashboard (sidebar, donut, card grid) and refuses its predictable opposite, the black terminal.
options.viewport: A ruled plate: station header with the observer's name and local time, then capacity read as sky cover in eighths — a real filled-fraction glyph, not a progress bar — with the four genera (Files, Media, Projects, Apps) as numbered specimens beneath, each with its plate number and measured extent.
options.risk: Renders as beige academic wallpaper if the ink and the notation are set timidly; the saturated end (oxblood, slate-blue overprint) has to carry it, not the paper.

options.label: Gate Board & Boarding Pass
options.lineage: airport departure boards and segmented boarding passes
options.thesis: Files as a board that reranks in place — a changed row moves and stays lit until you have noticed it. Uploads are segmented passes with sequence numbers.
options.viewport: A live board of files ordered by recency, changed rows holding an alert colour.
options.risk: A departure board is about imminent events, not a stored corpus. Wins on live upload and sync state; has no native carrier for capacity or for browsing 2,000 files of a codebase — which is most of this product.

options.label: Teletext Magazine
options.thesis: Every view has a three-digit page number you key directly; the whole app is addressable from the number row.
options.viewport: A 40-column page with a counting header and cyan figures on black.
options.risk: Fuses poorly here: it is black-ground, which the brief pinned against, and it is the predictable anti-SaaS move. Long file paths do not fit a 40-cell row.

options.label: Character Goods Roster
options.lineage: character goods catalogues — ranked mascots with name plates and birthdays
options.thesis: Profiles as a roster of characters, each with its own ribbon colour and personal furniture.
options.viewport: A pastel grid of profile characters with ruled name plates.
options.risk: Fuses poorly because a finite ranked roster cannot carry an unbounded file tree, and pastel mascots put an encrypted file server in a children's register.

canonCard.label: The category standard, played straight
canonCard.thesis: A conventional file-manager UI executed at a high craft level: left sidebar, breadcrumb, list with hover actions, a capacity bar, one accent colour.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar, breadcrumb, file rows, a capacity bar top-right.
canonCard.risk: It is what MiniCloud already is, and what every run would ship. Chosen deliberately it is a legitimate answer; chosen by default it is the rut.
